questions.question: You plan to replicate an Azure virtual machine in East US to West US 2 by using Azure Site Recovery. Where should you create the Recovery Services vault?

options.text: West US 2
options.why: Correct. For Azure-to-Azure disaster recovery, the vault is created in the target region.

options.text: East US
options.why: The vault must be in a different region from the source virtual machine.

options.text: Any region outside the United States
options.why: The vault is placed in the target region that you replicate to.

options.text: The vault location does not matter
options.why: Site Recovery requires the vault in the target region so that it is available if the source region fails.

questions.explanation: A cache storage account in the source region buffers changes before they are replicated.

questions.question: You must validate the disaster recovery plan for a replicated virtual machine every quarter. The validation must not affect production workloads or ongoing replication. What should you do?

options.text: Run a test failover to an isolated virtual network in the target region, and then run cleanup test failover
options.why: Correct. A test failover creates a copy of the virtual machine without affecting replication or production.

options.text: Run an unplanned failover and then fail back
options.why: A real failover affects production.

options.text: Disable replication and enable it again
options.why: This removes protection and requires initial replication again.

options.text: Run a test failover to the production virtual network in the target region
options.why: Using a production network can cause IP address conflicts. Use an isolated network.

questions.explanation: Test failovers can be run on single virtual machines or on recovery plans.

questions.question: A replicated virtual machine must be failed over to the secondary region during a regional outage. You must minimize the recovery time objective (RTO). Which recovery point should you select?

options.text: Latest processed
options.why: Correct. Latest processed uses a recovery point that has already been processed, so the failover is fastest.

options.text: Latest
options.why: Latest gives the lowest RPO but processes all pending data first, which increases RTO.

options.text: Latest app-consistent
options.why: This provides application consistency but may lose more data and is not chosen for the lowest RTO.

options.text: Custom
options.why: A custom point is used to go back to a specific time, not to minimize RTO.

questions.explanation: Latest gives the lowest RPO, Latest processed the lowest RTO, and Latest app-consistent an application-consistent state.

questions.question: You failed over a virtual machine from East US to West US 2 by using Azure Site Recovery. You must protect the virtual machine so that it can later be failed back to East US. Which three actions should you perform in sequence?

options.text: Commit the failover, run re-protect, and then fail back when East US is available
options.why: Correct. Commit finalizes the failover, re-protect replicates back to East US, and a failover back returns the workload.

options.text: Run re-protect, commit the failover, and then disable replication
options.why: Commit must happen before re-protect, and disabling replication removes protection.

options.text: Run cleanup test failover, commit the failover, and then re-protect
options.why: Cleanup applies only to test failovers.

options.text: Fail back immediately, commit the failover, and then re-protect
options.why: Fail back requires reverse replication, which re-protect provides.

questions.explanation: After failing back, commit and re-protect again to return to the original replication direction.

questions.question: A three-tier application runs on six virtual machines that replicate with Azure Site Recovery. During failover, the database virtual machines must start before the application servers, and a script must update a DNS record. What should you create?

options.text: A recovery plan with ordered groups and an Azure Automation runbook as a post action
options.why: Correct. Recovery plans fail over groups in order and can run scripts, runbooks and manual actions.

options.text: A replication policy with a shorter app-consistent snapshot frequency
options.why: The replication policy controls recovery points, not failover order.

options.text: Six separate test failovers
options.why: Test failovers validate the plan but do not define the order of a real failover.

options.text: An alert processing rule
options.why: Alert processing rules modify alerts, not failover steps.

questions.explanation: Run test failovers on the recovery plan to validate the order and the scripts.
